case_name: Magdy A. Ghaly and Laila Ryad v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Facts fully stipulated. Mr. Ghaly under 59 1/2 in 2018; laid off in 2018.

adjustments: unreported retirement income of $115,325 ($71,147 distribution + $44,178 deemed loan distribution)
10% additional tax on early distributions of $11,533
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Inclusion of retirement distributions and the 10% additional tax (asserted re-contribution in 2020 and use for medical/education/property-tax expenses)
conceded: Respondent conceded the sec. 6662(a) substantial understatement penalty

findings_of_fact.fact: Great-West processed withdrawal May 11, 2018; Form 1099-R reported $71,147 distribution with $14,229 withheld
findings_of_fact.snippet: indicating a distribution of $71,147 and withholding of $14,229.

findings_of_fact.fact: Mr. Ghaly defaulted in 2018 on a 2015 plan loan; second 1099-R reported deemed distribution of $44,178 (loan balance)
findings_of_fact.snippet: distribution of $44,178, the balance remaining on the loan.

findings_of_fact.fact: Mr. Ghaly had not attained age 59 1/2 at the time of the distributions
findings_of_fact.snippet: Mr. Ghaly had not attained the age of 59½ at the time of these distributions.

findings_of_fact.fact: Plan trust was a qualified trust under sec. 401(a); no exception to taxability established; 2020 contributions to new accounts do not offset 2018 inclusion
findings_of_fact.snippet: Mr. Ghaly does not dispute that his retirement plan trust was a qualified trust under section 401(a).

findings_of_fact.fact: Medical bill of $34,077 (dated Dec. 19, 2018) produced but no proof of payment; property taxes $6,238 paid irrelevant; distributions not used for any exception-qualifying expense
findings_of_fact.snippet: The withdrawal does not fit within any of the statutory exceptions, and the entire distribution is subject to the 10% additional tax.

issues.question: Does petitioners' 2018 gross income include $115,325 of retirement plan distributions (a $71,147 distribution and a $44,178 deemed distribution from a defaulted plan loan)?
issues.holding: Yes; both the actual and the deemed distribution are includible; later 2020 contributions to new accounts do not change 2018 inclusion
issues.computable_reason: Distributions from a 401(a) trust taxable under sec. 72 absent rollover; loan default deemed distribution under 72(p); amounts stipulated

issues.question: Are petitioners liable for the 10% additional tax under sec. 72(t) on the 2018 early distributions?
issues.holding: Yes; Mr. Ghaly under 59 1/2 and no statutory exception established; entire distribution subject to 10% additional tax
issues.computable_reason: Age under 59 1/2 and no qualifying exception found; tax is 10% of $115,325

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent as to the deficiency and for petitioners as to the accuracy-related penalty under section 6662(a).
decision.summary: Deficiency of $38,213 sustained including $115,325 distributions and $11,533 sec. 72(t) tax; 6662(a) penalty conceded by respondent

notes: Facts fully stipulated (Rule 122-like). Medical-expense exception (72(t)(2)(B)) failed for lack of proof of payment, a substantiation point, but as found the facts show no exception. Court assumed arguendo sec. 6201(d) burden of production met. Derived: 10% x $115,325 = $11,532.50, rounded $11,533.
